subject: Discovery: FastRetail PoC & integration plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery: FastRetail PoC & integration plan

Hi Alex / Priya 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed PoC/integration plan so we can align on owners and next steps.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Recommendation API 95th-p50 latency spikes during peak traffic (holiday windows) causing cart abandonment.
- Rising inference cost per query as models grow in complexity.
- Need for predictable performance, ability to route to lower-cost model variants, and stronger observability per-route.

Current stack you described:
- AWS (us-west-2), Node.js backend services, Kafka event pipeline, Postgres for user profiles.
- Client-side JS app + server-side rendering for personalization.

Success criteria for a successful PoC (from our discussion):
1) 95th percentile latency for recommendation endpoint < 200ms under target load.
2) End-to-end cost per query reduced to < $0.01 (target).
3) No customer data leaves us-west-2 (data residency requirement).
4) Observability: token-level latency and cost breakdowns for the PoC routes.

Proposed PoC scope & timeline (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): Access + allowlist, API keys, sample dataset + test harness.
- Week 1 (integration): Install Node.js SDK, basic routing + sample inference, verify API compatibility.
- Week 2 (performance): Load tests at expected QPS, tweak batching/cache/quantization settings.
- Week 3 (tuning): Iterate on model variant selection, cost/perf trade-offs.
- Week 4 (evaluation): Run acceptance tests against success criteria, produce results and next-step recommendations.

Owners (proposed):
- Ben Carter (Account Executive)  overall PoC owner, timelines, commercial.
- Marissa Cole (Solutions Engineering)  technical lead for integration/tests.
- Priya (FastRetail PM)  product/acceptance lead on your side.

A few quick questions to confirm before we lock dates:
1) Expected concurrent QPS for the recommendation endpoint (p95 target traffic).
2) Can you share a small sample of the event data (anonymized) we can use for the PoC test harness?
3) Any additional compliance or procurement contacts we should loop in now?

Attachments: integration_checklist.xlsx (simple checklist we use to collect network/credentials/SDK preferences).

Proposed kickoff: week of Oct 12th. Does that work for your team?

Thanks  look forward to moving quickly on this.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@fastretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: FastRetail PoC & integration plan

Thanks Ben  useful recap, appreciate the clarity. A few notes and answers below:

- Priorities: latency during peak windows (we've seen p95 jump from ~180ms to 600ms), and keeping incremental cost growth under control during holiday spikes. Observability is also high priority so we can correlate model changes to business metrics.
- Expected traffic: baseline 40 QPS, peak ~180 QPS (holiday peaks could go higher; we can simulate up to 500 QPS in the PoC).
- We can provide an anonymized sample events file and our network allowlist. Attaching both: fr_infra_network_requirements.pdf, fastretail_sample_events.json.
- SDK language: Node.js first choice (we also have a small Python infra team).
- Security: SOC 2 Type II is required for procurement. We'll need your SOC2 report and a brief note on data residency controls for us-west-2.

Couple product questions: does Redwood support streaming responses for incremental recommendation scoring, and do you maintain a KV cache to speed repeated prefix queries?

Procurement: I'll loop in Karen Li from procurement once we have the SOW/estimate.

Thanks  Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Personalization, FastRetail
alex.johnson@fastretail.com

Attachments: fr_infra_network_requirements.pdf, fastretail_sample_events.json

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: FastRetail PoC & integration plan

Thanks Alex  great signal on QPS and thank you for the attachments. Quick answers and a slightly more concrete plan with dates.

Security & compliance:
- We will share our SOC 2 Type II report and a short runbook on data residency controls (Redwood Hosted supports region pins; for Dedicated/Private we can support customer-managed KMS).

Product capabilities (short):
- Streaming: Yes  Redwood supports streaming responses over both SSE and WebSocket for incremental scoring.
- KV cache: Yes  we have prefix/KV caching to accelerate repeated queries and reduce token compute. Caching behavior and TTLs are configurable per-route.
- SDKs: Node.js (official), Python, Java. Node SDK includes helpers for SSE streaming and sample code for batching.
- API compatibility: REST endpoints, streaming via SSE/ws, authentication with API keys. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations.

Proposed PoC dates (aligned to your availability):
- Kickoff & access: Oct 12 (Week 0)
- Integration (Node SDK install + basic routing): Oct 12Oct 18
- Performance/load tests: Oct 19Oct 25
- Tuning & model variants: Oct 26Nov 1
- Evaluation & results: Nov 2Nov 8

Owners & tasks:
- Ben Carter (PoC coordination, timelines, commercial).
- Marissa Cole (SE lead  integration, test harness, perf runs).
- Stephanie Nguyen (Observability + billing metrics, run dashboards).
- FastRetail: Priya (PM) and Alex (product lead) to validate acceptance tests; Karen (procurement) for SOW review.

Deliverables we'll provide before kickoff:
- PoC SOW & success criteria doc (attached: FastRetail_SOW_draft.pdf).
- Quickstart repo & Node SDK example for recommendation endpoint. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cExampleDriveLink

Actions for FastRetail before Oct 8:
1) Share anonymized sample dataset (you noted this is possible)  we'll use it for the test harness.
2) Provide network allowlist details (we received your doc  thank you).
3) Confirm list of procurement/legal contacts to loop in for SOW.

If that timeline looks good, we'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff on Oct 12 to get keys and access configured.

Thanks  looping marissa and stephanie to pick up technical threads.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: FastRetail_SOW_draft.pdf
